name: QTS Eemshaven data center campus
summary: Data center campus of Blackstone-backed QTS Data Centers at Huibertgatweg 2 in the Eemshaven port area of Groningen, the Netherlands. QTS bought the existing, then vacant 20 gross MW building in 2019 and in July 2025 was reported to be investing EUR 1.4 billion to expand the campus and double its regional capacity. QTS's campus page now describes up to 18 hectares, three facilities and 200 MW of planned capacity delivered in phases: the first building is operational, the second is in phased delivery and the third is under construction.

location.note: Point for the 'QTS Eemshaven Netherlands Data Center' building (OSM way 455499803, Huibertgatweg) from the local OpenStreetMap layer, matching the address on QTS's campus page. The layer also maps a QTS new build about 350 m to the north-west; the full 18-hectare campus boundary is not published.

metrics.note: QTS describes this as planned gross renewable capacity delivered in phases; the undated campus page was read on 2026-10-09.
Built-out capacity of about 20 gross MW in the building QTS bought, which was vacant at the time.
The Tech Capital also gives USD 1.5 billion as the equivalent.
Development scope including associated works and structures.

milestones.note: QTS closed the purchase of the Eemshaven and Groningen data centers for about USD 44 million including closing costs.
Groningen Seaports' March 2025 newsletter listed construction of a new QTS data center among port projects.
EUR 1.4 billion expansion reported; Structure Research cited local media saying a second data center was under construction.

power_sources.description: On-site substation; QTS says renewable-sourced power is available.

notes: Status, the 200 MW, 18-hectare and three-building figures and job counts come from QTS's undated campus page, so status_as_of is the access date. The EUR 1.4 billion figure comes from the visible lede of a paywalled Tech Capital article; Dutch press coverage of the expansion (including a 2029 timeline and the name EEMSDC2) could not be opened, so it is not recorded. QTS's 2019 release said the site neighbours a 500+ MW campus of a hyperscale cloud provider. The campus page also mentions a partnership with WarmteStad to share residual heat from QTS's Netherlands data centers, without saying it covers Eemshaven.
